header: It started with a theodolite bought at an auction and a shop that had stood empty for two years
lead: Gerhard Tulln opened Aubruck in a former butcher's shop on Bahnhofstraße because the rent was low and the floor was level enough to check an instrument on.
bodytext:
He had spent eleven years at the cadastral office in Sandau and left it the week his second child was born, which everyone told him was the wrong order to do things in. The first year he worked alone. The jobs were garden boundaries and the odd subdivision, and he did the drawing at the kitchen table after the children were in bed because the shop had no heating until October 1995.

The office survived its first winter on a single contract: the Nauwang sewer, four kilometres of it, surveyed between January and March in weather that broke two tripods. The municipality paid late and in three parts. Gerhard used to say that the job taught him everything he needed to know about running a business, most of it about invoicing.

By 2002 there were nine people and the shop had become too small. By 2010 there were three offices, which was never a plan — Nauwang and Kettbach both began as somebody working from home who was closer to the sites than Hollerau was. He handed the office to Marlene Ostermann in 2016 and still comes in on Thursdays to argue about field books.
caption: Gerhard Tulln outside the Bahnhofstraße shop, spring 1995.
author: Gerhard Tulln
